title: Platform systems & services playbook: how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, roadmap, team wiki
author: Elena Garcia
content:
Summary
=======
This page is the authoritative platform engineering playbook for Redwood Inference: it consolidates systems & services inventory, operational how-tos, dashboard and alert guidance, standard runbooks, recent retrospectives and the next 3-quarter roadmap. It is intended for oncall engineers, platform owners, SREs, and anyone making changes to platform services.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all platform-owned services in the `platform-` and `infra-` namespaces (Kubernetes clusters, control-plane services, autoscalers, observability pipelines, and key shared services such as cache, auth, and routing).
- Excludes model-serving workloads owned by eng-serving-runtime (see related pages).

Ownership and contact
---------------------
- Platform product lead: Marcus Lee (marcus@redwood.ai)
- Platform engineering manager: Priya Nair (priya@redwood.ai)
- Oncall rotation: platform-oncall@redwood.ai (see /confluence/eng-platform/platform-rotation-schedule for schedule)
- Primary Slack: #platform-ops, #platform-oncall

Systems & services inventory (high level)
----------------------------------------
The table below lists critical platform services, owners, and SLOs. Use this as the canonical reference for runbook delegation and alert routing.

| Service name | Purpose | Owner | SLO (p99 latency / availability) | Pager? | Notes |
|--------------|---------|-------|-----------------------------------|--------|-------|
| platform-api | Internal control plane API for deployments | eng-platform-api | p99 < 200ms, availability 99.95% | yes | Handles rollout API and feature flags |
| platform-queue | Job queue for platform tasks (batch/cron) | eng-platform-systems | p99 < 5s for enqueue, availability 99.9% | no | Backed by Redis cluster |
| platform-grafana | Dashboards and templating | eng-observability | N/A | no | Managed Grafana with RBAC |
| platform-alerts | Alert manager + routing | eng-sre | N/A | yes | Routes to #platform-oncall and PagerDuty |
| platform-cache | Shared in-memory prefix cache for deployments | eng-platform-cache | p99 < 10ms, availability 99.9% | yes | Sharded Redis; autoscale script in repo |

Service ownership MUST be kept up-to-date in the team wiki. If you change ownership, add an entry to the `platform-owners` repo and notify #platform-ops.

How-tos (top-level operational procedures)
------------------------------------------
1) Create a new platform dashboard
   1. Navigate to Grafana -> Create -> Dashboard
   2. Use `platform-dashboard` JSON template from `/repos/platform/dashboards/templates`
   3. Replace variables: cluster, env, service_name
   4. Add panels: CPU, MEM, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, request rate, queue backlog
   5. Set time range to 6h default; add refresh 15s for critical services
   6. Save to folder: `Platform / <service_name>` and set viewer ACL to `platform-read`

   Example CLI export: `curl -sS -X POST "$GRAFANA/api/dashboards/db" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GRAFANA_TOKEN" -d @platform-dashboard.json`

2) Create an alert rule (Prometheus + Alertmanager)
   - Use templated rule format in `/repos/platform/alerts/common-rules.yaml`
   - Standard severity labels: severity=critical, severity=warning
   - Critical alert example: `expr: increase(http_requests_error_total{job="platform-api"}[5m]) > 5`
   - Recommended thresholds: error-rate > 1% (critical if sustained 5m), p99 latency > 500ms (critical)
   - After adding rule, open PR against `infra-monitoring` and tag `eng-sre` + `eng-platform` reviewers.

3) Tune alert paging policy
   - Edit `platform-alerts` route in Alertmanager: critical -> PagerDuty -> oncall schedule; warning -> Slack -> #platform-ops
   - For flapping alerts enable `for: 5m` and `labels: severity: warning` until mitigated.

Runbooks (standardized, step-by-step)
-------------------------------------
A. platform-api degraded (high latency)
1. Triage
   - Check Grafana dashboard: p99 latency, error rate, CPU/memory, DB connections, queue length.
   - Query Prometheus: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="platform-api"}[5m])) by (le))`
2. Quick mitigation (choose applicable)
   - If CPU saturation on pods: scale deployment `kubectl scale deployment platform-api --replicas=$((current+2)) -n platform`
   - If DB is slow: check RDS metrics; roll back recent schema migration if newly deployed
   - If KV cache is thrashing: clear prefix cache for the service `platform-cache clear --prefix platform-api` (use with caution)
3. Post-incident
   - Record timeline in postmortem template. Assign action owners and target ETA for fixes.

B. Cache storm / eviction cascade
1. Identify the pattern: sudden drop in cache hit rate (Grafana panel `cache.hit_rate` < 60%) and simultaneous increase in backend requests.
2. Mitigation steps:
   - Temporarily increase cache replicas: `kubectl patch sts platform-cache --patch "{"spec":{"replicas":5}}" -n infra`
   - Apply rate-limits on platform-api to throttle cold-cache traffic: update `rate-limit` config map for platform-api routes
   - Enable read-through cache fallback in config `features.read_through_fallback=true` for 30 minutes
3. Long-term actions: increase cache capacity, improve prefix sharding, add grace TTLs for evicted keys.

C. GPU node OOM / model-serving impact (interacts with Dedicated)
1. Check cluster autoscaler events and GPU node logs.
2. Cordon affected node: `kubectl cordon <node>` and create eviction pod drain with `--ignore-daemonsets`
3. If autoscaler fails to provision: escalate to infra-team and open ticket with cloud provider with relevant events and debug logs.

Dashboards & Alerts guidance (detailed)
--------------------------------------
- SLOs and Error Budgets:
  - Core platform API: 99.95% availability monthly; error budget burn rate > 3x for 1h -> page eng-sre and product manager.
  - Non-critical background jobs: 99.5%
- Standard dashboard panels (must include): request rate (rps), 50/95/99 latency, error count and rate, retransmit/backoff occurrences, CPU/MEM, heap growth (if JVM), DB connection pool usage, queue backlog, cache hit rate.
- Alert priority mapping:
  - critical: immediate paging, runbook required, create incident in Incident DB
  - warning: Slack alert to #platform-ops, track in triage board
  - info: for engagement / internal visibility only

Alert tuning checklist:
- Ensure `for:` is set to avoid flapping (5m for critical thresholds unless business-critical).
- Group by `service_name` and `cluster` to reduce noise.
- Annotate alerts with runbook links: `runbook_url` label.

Runbook lifecycle and ownership
------------------------------
- Every runbook must have an owner and last_updated date in the top metadata block.
- Runbooks are reviewed quarterly during oncall handover. Break/fix owners must acknowledge post-incident changes within 5 business days.

Retrospectives (recent highlights)
----------------------------------
- Incident: cache-thrash-2025-12-03
  - Summary: A sudden traffic shift caused prefix collisions and mass evictions, increasing backend load and causing platform-api throttles.
  - Root cause: insufficient sharding logic for a new customer deployment and missing grace TTLs.
  - Actions: implement dynamic prefix sharder (PR #342), add grace TTL feature flag, add `cache.hit_rate` alerts. Owner: Tomás Álvarez.

- Incident: grafana-outage-2026-01-07
  - Summary: Grafana upgrades failed due to an incompatible plugin causing dashboards to 500.
  - Actions: pinned Grafana to stable chart, added test job to validate plugin compatibility during staging upgrades. Owner: Priya Nair.

Roadmap (next 3 quarters)
------------------------
Q1 2026:
- Finish platform API refactor (rolling restart support, faster delta updates).
- Launch templated dashboards + onboarding flow for new services.
Q2 2026:
- Cache autoscaling alpha with predictive scaling based on traffic patterns.
- Improved alert classification (ML-assisted de-duplication).
Q3 2026:
- Private deployment observability kit (air-gapped Grafana + offline alerting) for Redwood Private customers.

Team wiki and onboarding checklist
---------------------------------
- New platform engineer checklist:
  1. Read this playbook and sign off in #platform-ops.
  2. Complete platform oncall shadowing (2 weeks).
  3. Add your GitHub handle to `platform-owners` and claim 1 runbook.
  4. Complete Grafana and Prometheus training modules (internal LMS link).
- Documentation conventions:
  - File names: use kebab-case, include year and quarter when applicable.
  - Runbooks: short name, summary line, owner, last_updated, step-by-step, postmortem link.
  - Dashboards: versioned JSON in `repos/platform/dashboards` and an immutable snapshot on major changes.

Change control and rollout checklist
----------------------------------
1. Feature or infra change must have a PR with changelog and risk assessment.
2. For any change affecting SLOs, attach an SLO impact assessment and notify eng-sre and product.
3. Canary deployment: 5% traffic for 30 minutes -> 25% for 1 hour -> 100% if stable.
4. If canary fails, automatic rollback is configured in the deployment pipeline with a 5-min window for manual override.

Appendix: useful commands and links
----------------------------------
- Dashboards repo: git@internal:redwood/platform/dashboards.git
- Monitoring repo: git@internal:redwood/infra-monitoring.git
- Grafana API token helper: `scripts/grafana/create-token.sh --service platform-api`
- Query examples:
  - p99 latency: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="platform-api"}[5m])) by (le))`
  - cache hit rate: `sum(rate(cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(cache_requests_total[5m]))`

If you find gaps or missing runbooks, file a ticket in the `platform-docs` board and assign `eng-platform` as owner.

Last review notes:
- Reviewed during Q4 2025 platform retro. Action items tracked in /confluence/eng-platform/retrospectives-2025-q4.
